property_summary: For any caller and any candidate address, a successful call to setOwner must make c.owner() equal that candidate address; the mutant never updates owner, so this breaks for any candidate different from the current owner.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): `vm.assume` rejected too many inputs (65536 allowed)

property_summary: For any candidate address distinct from the deployer, a successful call by the current owner to setOwner(candidate) must make c.owner() equal the candidate; the mutant never updates owner, so it fails for every such candidate.

For any owner caller and any proposed address distinct from that caller, a successful setOwner(proposed) must set owner to exactly the proposed address; the buggy version instead sets owner to the caller, violating this for every proposed != caller.

After transferring ownership to a new owner, that new owner can set the owner to a further distinct address (ownership is transferable by the current owner to any chosen address); the mutant instead pins owner to whoever calls, so it never reaches the chosen second address.
For any caller who is the current owner and any address a, after setOwner(a) the owner equals a; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), violating this for any a != address(this).

For any admissible new owner a (a != address(c)), a call from the current owner to setOwner(a) must make c.owner() equal a; the mutant instead sets owner to address(this), so c.owner() != a for any a != address(c).
Only the current owner can change ownership: for any non-owner caller, setOwner reverts and owner is unchanged, while the buggy version lets any caller overwrite owner.

For any caller address, only a call from the current owner may succeed in changing owner; the buggy inverted check makes calls from non-owners succeed (and owner calls revert), so owner changes to a fuzzed new owner differ.

For any caller, setOwner may only succeed when the caller is the current owner (and then owner becomes the given address); the buggy version lets any non-owner caller succeed and take ownership, which the fuzzer finds with a non-owner actor.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): only current owner may change owner

property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner and any new owner address, a successful setOwner call must return true; the mutant returns false for every successful call, so the assertion fails.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): successful setOwner by owner must return true

property_summary: For any input address, a call to setOwner by the current owner must return true (the success flag is always true on success); the mutant deletes the return so it returns false, breaking the rule.
For any address a, calling setOwner(a) as the owner must leave owner == a; the mutant writes address(0) instead, so owner() != a (for a != 0), and thereafter it even locks itself out.
For any caller who is the owner, setOwner to any address succeeds and returns true; the mutant returns false instead, breaking this rule.
For any address passed by the owner, setOwner succeeds and stores exactly that address as owner; the mutant wrongly reverts when the chosen address is address(0).

For any address chosen by the owner, the contract must revert when setOwner is called by a non-owner, and after any successful setOwner the public owner getter equals the new owner — the mutant breaks this by reverting on setOwner(address(0)) which the reference accepts.
For any fuzzed address a, calling setOwner(a) as the current owner must unconditionally make c.owner() equal a; the mutant breaks this by reverting when a == address(0), leaving owner unchanged.

For any caller value seed, the owner can set the owner to address(uint160(seed)) — including address(0) — and the public owner getter then equals it; the mutant reverts on address(0), leaving owner unchanged, breaking the rule.
For any admissible new owner, a successful setOwner call must return true; the mutant returns owner != _owner, which is always false, so it violates this for every input.
For any input, setOwner called by the current owner never returns false (it always succeeds and updates the owner); the mutant breaks this by returning false when the new owner is the zero address.

For every admissible address, calling setOwner from the current owner completes without reverting, returns true, and leaves owner equal to that address; the mutant instead returns false and leaves owner unchanged when the new owner is address(0).
